records.question_fingerprint: Interpret an MLD diagnostic with one active link versus three links and isolate model/radio/security/profile prerequisites.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: One Wi-Fi 7 MLD client connected to a single logical SSID across three radio links, with controller/WTP profile mapping and standalone-authentication branch.

records.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 API/HTTPS SMS Gateway: connector-driven notifications and sponsor LDAP group mapping
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds API/HTTPS SMS gateway integration alongside legacy Mail-to-SMS, including cloud-provider integration such as Twilio and LDAP group mapping for sponsors; notifications can target administrators, guests, and users.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC event or user workflow selects a notification recipient; Email/SMS service connector routes the message through configured HTTPS provider integration; provider accepts request and delivers through its SMS network; sponsor eligibility is derived from configured LDAP group mapping.
records.failure_class: Connector disabled or misconfigured, provider authentication/endpoint issue, outbound HTTPS/DNS failure, recipient normalization or provider quota failure, or sponsor group mapping not matching the intended LDAP group.
records.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC Email/SMS connector configuration and event/notification records show message dispatch; provider-side request logs distinguish API acceptance from carrier delivery; sponsor group mapping can be compared with LDAP membership.
records.remediation_path: Configure the 9.4 Email/SMS connector using the provider-supported settings; validate outbound DNS/TLS and provider credentials; test with a controlled recipient; verify provider acceptance and delivery separately; confirm sponsor LDAP group mapping and membership.
records.question_fingerprint: Separate FortiNAC notification generation, HTTPS provider acceptance, carrier delivery, and LDAP sponsor authorization.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC event/guest workflow and LDAP sponsor group feed a recipient/connector decision, then HTTPS SMS provider and carrier delivery with acknowledgment boundary.

records.lesson_subject: FortiLink integration credential planes: REST API token, SSH/CLI, SNMPv3, and separate RADIUS enforcement
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.5+ uses a FortiGate REST API token in addition to—not instead of—System Administrator SSH/CLI and SNMPv3 for FortiLink-managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP inventory, L2/L3 polling and VLAN control; RADIUS remains the endpoint-authentication/dynamic-VLAN plane. Current FortiOS releases have version-specific token transport requirements.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F polls FortiGate REST API with token for managed inventory/MAC/VLAN state; SSH/CLI supplies FortiSwitch discovery and command functions; SNMPv3 supplies monitoring/traps; RADIUS handles endpoint authentication and CoA; token URL-parameter compatibility differs by FortiOS release and the legacy rest-api-key-url-query command is removed in FortiOS 8.0.
records.failure_class: REST token missing/invalid or incompatible with FortiOS token transport, CLI credential removed so switches are not discovered, SNMPv3 removed so monitoring/traps disappear, or RADIUS mistakenly expected to be replaced by API credentials.
records.evidence_pattern: FortiNAC FortiGate Model Configuration shows API token plus CLI/SNMP settings; Network Inventory shows FortiSwitch/FortiAP models; output.master shows REST API status and polling errors; community scenario notes token clearing after VLAN change when legacy query-parameter setting is absent.
records.remediation_path: Create dedicated REST API Admin with minimum read or read/write scope and trusted host; add token to FortiGate model; retain CLI and SNMPv3; keep RADIUS separately; validate FortiOS/FortiNAC compatibility and do not apply the legacy rest-api-key-url-query workaround to FortiOS 8.0 where the command is removed.
records.question_fingerprint: Given missing switch discovery, failed VLAN changes, or absent SNMP traps, map each symptom to the correct independent credential/protocol plane.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F connected to FortiGate/FortiLink with three parallel REST API, SSH/CLI and SNMPv3 management channels plus a separate endpoint-to-RADIUS authentication path.

records.lesson_subject: SCEP with Microsoft Intune and Entra ID-backed EAP-TLS: OAuth challenge generation, certificate binding, and SAML group-to-RADIUS policy
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 adds an Intune option for SCEP challenge-password generation using an Azure Directory OAuth server; remote SAML users can carry certificate bindings, SAML user groups can carry RADIUS attributes, and SAML realms/remote group filters can participate in RADIUS policy selection.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Intune requests SCEP enrollment; FortiAuthenticator uses Azure Directory OAuth/tenant ID to generate challenge password and issues certificate from local CA; EAP-TLS presents client certificate; remote SAML user certificate binding resolves identity; SAML group filter and RADIUS attributes supply authorization in the selected realm/policy.
records.failure_class: SCEP disabled or HTTP interface access missing, invalid/expired CA, OAuth server lacks Azure tenant ID, unsupported Azure Government tenant, certificate binding mismatch, SAML group filter absent from RADIUS realm/policy, or missing RADIUS attributes.
records.evidence_pattern: SCEP Enrollment Requests shows Pending/Approved/Rejected and issuer/subject; certificate chain and SAN/UPN binding identify the enrolled endpoint/user; RADIUS session and policy logs show realm, matched group and returned attributes.
records.remediation_path: Enable SCEP and HTTP on serving interface; validate local CA; configure Azure Directory OAuth with tenant ID; choose InTune challenge-password generation; configure remote SAML user certificate bindings and group RADIUS attributes; add SAML realm/group filter to RADIUS policy; test enrollment and EAP-TLS separately.
records.question_fingerprint: Trace a certificate from Intune SCEP issuance through remote SAML identity binding into RADIUS group authorization without confusing enrollment with authentication.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Intune SCEP enrollment/OAuth/CA issuance path converges with EAP-TLS certificate presentation, SAML user/group binding and RADIUS policy attribute response.

records.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 agentless web launchers: browser tab-sharing consent, recording upload, and launcher limitations
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Agentless mode launches supported web-based secrets without FortiClient or the Privileged Access Agent browser extension; automatic mode prioritizes FortiClient, then extension, then agentless; Web Browsing is excluded, Firefox unsupported, and macOS requires screen/audio recording permission.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches supported web secret; browser asks permission to share FortiPAM tab; session header shows lifetime and Stop sharing; stopping sharing or closing tab terminates session and uploads video; native launchers are unaffected by the agentless selector.
records.failure_class: Unsupported browser or launcher, tab-sharing consent not granted, macOS screen/system-audio permission missing, Web RDP resolution expectation, or assuming agentless mode supports native/Web Browsing launchers.
records.evidence_pattern: Banner shows selected Agentless mode; browser tab displays Allow prompt and Stop sharing header; session lifetime is visible; video appears in logs after Stop sharing; browser warning appears when extension absent.
records.remediation_path: Use Chrome or Edge and a supported web launcher; select Agentless explicitly or verify automatic priority; grant tab sharing; on macOS grant Screen & System Audio Recording; use Stop sharing to close and upload recording; use supported mode for Web Browsing/native launchers.
records.question_fingerprint: Determine why a Web SSH/RDP session opens but its recording is missing, and distinguish agentless launcher support from Web Browsing/native launchers.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM mode selector to Chrome/Edge tab-sharing permission, proxied web launcher session and recording-upload branch; unsupported launcher/browser exits.

records.lesson_subject: AWS Security Hub integration: regional findings ingestion, SDK credential scope, and FortiSIEM discovery
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM 7.5.1 integrates AWS Security Hub through the AWS Security Hub SDK/PHP V3 SDK; Security Hub findings are region-scoped and FortiSIEM credentials can specify multiple AWS region codes for discovery and ingestion.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Enable Security Hub in each intended AWS region; create IAM access key with documented permissions; create FortiSIEM credential using Device Type Amazon AWS Security Hub and Access Protocol AWS Security Hub SDK with region list; test connectivity; run AWS Scan discovery; ingest findings as FortiSIEM events.
records.failure_class: Security Hub disabled in one or more regions, wrong region code, insufficient IAM permissions, invalid access key, incorrect credential-to-region association, or assuming one region's findings cover all accounts/regions.
records.evidence_pattern: FortiSIEM credential shows AWS Security Hub SDK and region list; Test Connectivity succeeds; CMDB discovery records AWS Security Hub; Resources > Event Types contains AWS Sechub types and incoming finding events.
records.remediation_path: Enable Security Hub in every intended region; validate IAM permissions against Fortinet's documented integration requirements and least privilege; use correct region codes in credential; test connectivity; rerun AWS Scan; confirm findings exist in each region before troubleshooting FortiSIEM parsing.
records.question_fingerprint: Explain why a working Security Hub integration reports findings from one region but not another and identify the regional enablement boundary.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple AWS regions each with Security Hub findings feed a single FortiSIEM AWS SDK credential/discovery path, then CMDB and event/rule/report pipeline.

records.lesson_subject: Inline-CASB application detection and SaaS tenant restriction: deep inspection, HTTP header insertion, and per-application overrides
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Inline-CASB uses IPS protocol decoders to detect SaaS application traffic on HTTP/1.0, 1.1 and 2.0, including non-standard ports; SSL deep inspection exposes HTTPS payloads for application-control decisions and Web Filter Inline-CASB can insert/remove tenant-restriction HTTP headers.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint traffic enters FortiSASE policy; deep inspection terminates/re-establishes TLS using trusted FortiSASE CA; application decoder identifies SaaS; category action allow/monitor/block is evaluated with per-app override; optional Web Filter header rule modifies matching HTTP request; vendor enforces tenant identifier.
records.failure_class: Certificate inspection used instead of deep inspection, endpoint does not trust FortiSASE CA, profile group not attached to matching policy, unsupported QUIC/HTTP version, malformed tenant ID/header, or traffic bypasses FortiSASE.
records.evidence_pattern: Web Filter with Inline-CASB logs show application match and inserted header under Change Headers/Details; FortiView Cloud Applications shows access attempts; corporate tenant works while disallowed account is rejected by SaaS vendor.
records.remediation_path: Enable SSL deep inspection and deploy trusted CA; enable Inline-CASB application control and Web Filter in the same security profile group; attach profile to matching policy; define FQDN destination group and exact vendor header; block QUIC where required; validate UUID and ensure traffic traverses FortiSASE.
records.question_fingerprint: Differentiate application-category blocking from tenant-restriction header insertion and diagnose why certificate inspection cannot expose the required HTTP header.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remote endpoint through FortiSASE TLS inspection and IPS application decoder, category/override policy, optional HTTP header insertion, SaaS tenant decision and logs.

records.lesson_subject: SD-WAN Setup Wizard: license-gated generation of zone, members, SLA and service rule with a separate default-route step
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN Setup Wizard creates a zone, up to two member interfaces, gateway/cost/fallback priority, Performance SLA and SD-WAN service rule; it requires valid SD-WAN Underlay and Application Monitoring licenses and does not create the required default static route automatically.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Wizard gathers underlay interfaces and gateway/priority; creates or selects zone and members; selects FortiGuard or manual SLA; creates service rule or uses implicit rule; review applies generated objects; administrator separately adds static route to SD-WAN zone.
records.failure_class: Missing license hides wizard, more than two underlays exceeds wizard scope, wrong cost/fallback priority affects path selection, SLA target unsuitable, or omitted default static route leaves traffic on another route.
records.evidence_pattern: Network > SD-WAN shows created zone/members/health-check/rule; Network > Static Routes must separately show default route to SD-WAN zone; SLA status and session route confirm actual steering.
records.remediation_path: Confirm both required licenses; use wizard only for two-underlay bootstrap; inspect generated members, gateway, cost, priority, SLA target and service strategy; add the default static route manually; verify firewall policy and route selection before testing application steering.
records.question_fingerprint: Identify why a completed wizard creates SD-WAN objects but traffic still follows the old default route, and distinguish SLA state from route installation.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Wizard stages from licensed underlay selection through zone/member creation, SLA, service rule and review, followed by a separate static-route/policy gate to traffic forwarding.

records.lesson_subject: FortiOS 8.0 TLS 1.3 IPsec transport over TCP: per-VDOM enablement, Auto fallback, certificate trust and upgrade behavior
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 adds TLS 1.3 as an IPsec IKE/ESP TCP encapsulation transport; ike-tcp-service and ike-tls-service are per-VDOM gates; TLS mode is FortiGate-to-FortiGate.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IKEv2 begins over UDP; with TCP/TLS services enabled and transport Auto, the initiator can retry over TCP/TLS; IKE and ESP are carried inside TLS; peer certificate validation precedes Phase 2 and normal firewall-policy traffic.
records.failure_class: UDP blocked but fallback disabled; TLS listener disabled on one peer; untrusted or mismatched certificate; FortiClient incorrectly expected to use the new FortiGate-to-FortiGate TLS mode; post-upgrade static Auto tunnel conversion misunderstood.
records.evidence_pattern: IKE gateway output identifies transport and peer; IKE debug shows TLS handshake/certificate result; packet capture shows TCP/TLS; established SA does not prove routes or firewall policies pass application traffic.
records.remediation_path: Enable TCP/TLS services on both peers; use IKEv2 and Auto; import correct CA and use matching peer identity; validate listener/port, route and policy separately; review upgrade conversion; do not conflate RFC8229 TCP encapsulation with the new TLS mode.
records.question_fingerprint: separate UDP negotiation, TCP fallback gates, TLS certificate validation and post-tunnel policy failure from their distinct evidence.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: two FortiGates, UDP-first path, TCP/TLS 1.3 fallback, mutual peer trust, IKE/ESP encapsulation and separate protected-data policy path.

records.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 ADOM upgrade readiness: syntax compatibility, database conversion and remote-certificate preflight
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: ADOM version is the FortiOS syntax/database schema version, not FortiManager firmware; readiness checks device configurations for unsupported syntax before ADOM object conversion and reports blockers without repairing them.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select same-version ADOMs; readiness evaluates device/VDOM syntax; exported report drives remediation; ADOM upgrade converts schema/objects; device resync and install preview validate the resulting target syntax.
records.failure_class: Unsupported device firmware or syntax; malformed remote certificate PEM wrapper; mixed ADOM versions assumed compatible; workspace ADOM not locked; object conversion succeeds but later install exposes a device-specific syntax issue.
records.evidence_pattern: Readiness report identifies exact incompatible objects; ADOM support matrix establishes version compatibility; Remote Certificate and Where Used reveal SAML/PKI dependencies; successful readiness does not guarantee install success.
records.remediation_path: Back up FortiManager; verify lowest device firmware; lock workspace ADOM; run readiness; repair invalid syntax and PEM delimiters without changing certificate bytes; upgrade supported ADOM versions together; resync devices and run install preview before production install.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish FortiManager firmware, ADOM schema, managed-device firmware and malformed shared certificate data.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager above multiple ADOM schema lanes; device/VDOM syntax checks feed readiness report; remediation gate precedes schema conversion and device resync/install.

records.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 FortiMQ connector: ADOM-scoped indicator delivery and Cloud Fabric Feed enforcement
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer 8.0 FortiMQ connector is a disabled-by-default cloud connector that transmits blocked IP, URL, domain or MAC indicators through block_indicator playbook; FortiGate retrieves them as Cloud-based Fabric Feeds; connector scope follows source ADOM.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Logs reach FortiAnalyzer; analyst blocks an indicator; playbook posts to FortiMQ; FortiGate syncs cloud feed; feed object is referenced by a firewall/security profile; unblock reverses indicator state.
records.failure_class: Connector disabled; FortiGate and FortiAnalyzer not under same FortiCare account; feed sync disabled; ADOM mismatch; indicator submission mistaken for enforcement; existing FortiManager connector assumed to supersede FortiMQ.
records.evidence_pattern: Active connector proves API health; playbook run proves submission; FortiGate feed contents/last-update prove retrieval; policy/profile reference and traffic test prove enforcement.
records.remediation_path: Enable connector in the correct Fabric/FortiGate ADOM; confirm same FortiCare account and FortiGate cloud-feed sync; validate indicator type and scope; inspect playbook; confirm feed population and policy reference; disable FortiMQ only when deliberately using the FortiManager path.
records.question_fingerprint: separate connector health, ADOM scope, indicator submission, feed retrieval and actual policy enforcement.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiGate logs to FortiAnalyzer ADOM; analyst indicator to playbook to FortiMQ cloud; FortiGate feed sync to external-feed object to policy.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch egress QoS: CoS/DSCP trust maps, eight queues, scheduler weights and congestion drops
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch maps ingress 802.1p CoS or IP DSCP into one of eight egress queues; trust selection determines classification; strict, round-robin and weighted scheduling govern service; tail-drop and model-dependent RED/WRED control congestion.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress trust selects CoS or DSCP map; classification selects queue; optional ACL remarking changes markings; egress policy selects scheduling and rate/drop behavior; policy binds to ports; scheduler transmits or drops under congestion.
records.failure_class: Wrong trust map selects default queue; both CoS and DSCP trust cause DSCP precedence; queue 7 oversubscribed by data; strict scheduling starves lower queues; model lacks configured min-rate/WRED/ECN options.
records.evidence_pattern: dot1p/dscp maps and port QoS policy show intent; switch QoS counters show queue occupancy/drop behavior; compare ingress markings and selected queue under controlled congestion; CPU internal queues are not identical to port queue counters.
records.remediation_path: Choose one trust source per port; map DSCP/CoS intentionally; reserve queue 7 for control; use WRR where starvation is unacceptable; verify model feature matrix; inspect per-port queue counters before tuning.
records.question_fingerprint: trace voice/data packet classification to egress queue and scheduler while distinguishing port queue 7 from CPU control queues.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: ingress CoS/DSCP trust -> eight egress queues -> strict/RR/WRR scheduler -> tail-drop/WRED/ECN congestion branch -> egress.

records.lesson_subject: FortiAP 8.0 wireless packet sniffer: radio-channel capture, frame filters and browser-streamed PCAP
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A FortiAP profile places one radio in packet-sniffer mode; captures over-the-air management, control and data frames on a selected channel/channel width with optional station-MAC and frame-type filters; FortiGate GUI streams capture to browser and does not persist PCAP on FortiGate.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Select radio in WTP profile; configure sniffer mode/channel/width/buffer/MAC/frame filters; apply profile; start one AP capture; packets stream to browser; stop and save PCAP locally; analyze 802.11 management/control/data frames.
records.failure_class: Wrong radio/channel/width misses frames; filter excludes target; one AP capture already running; operator changes radio mode before exporting temporary capture; browser stream mistaken for FortiGate-stored PCAP.
records.evidence_pattern: Profile shows capture settings; AP status confirms radio mode; live stream and saved PCAP expose beacon/probe/control/data, retries, rate and RSSI; no frames proves only that the configured radio/filter/channel did not observe them.
records.remediation_path: Match channel and width to affected BSS; use separate APs for simultaneous band captures; begin with broad filters; run one capture at a time; save PCAP before changing radio mode; use separate CAPWAP capture when controller transport is suspect.
records.question_fingerprint: choose over-the-air radio capture versus CAPWAP transport capture and identify where the PCAP is stored.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP radio/channel/filter boundary -> live browser stream -> local PCAP analyzer; separate CAPWAP control/data path.

records.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 MDM service connectors: host registration, health state and polling fan-out
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 MDM Service Connector uses vendor API inventory and health data to register/refresh hosts; optional on-demand registration, automatic inventory polling, application inventory, health revalidation, deletion reconciliation and Manager fan-out are distinct controls.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Unknown host reaches captive portal -> on-demand MDM lookup -> host registration; scheduled poll -> API authentication -> host inventory/health update -> host database -> NAC policy; FortiNAC Manager may poll once and distribute records to managed servers.
records.failure_class: Stale Last Successful Poll; delegated/application permission mismatch; unsupported proxy path; host identity mismatch; on-demand registration disabled; aggressive health/application polling throttles MDM; Remove Hosts deletes still-needed host records.
records.evidence_pattern: Last Poll versus Last Successful Poll; Test Connection; Poll Now; service-connector audit log; MDM-managed host record and health fields; Manager propagation to the server controlling the port. A successful connection test does not prove host registration or policy enforcement.
records.remediation_path: Use application permissions where supported; validate Request URL, application ID, secret/certificate and vendor API permissions; account for no-proxy constraint; enable on-demand registration for unknown hosts; use measured poll intervals; test Remove Hosts in staging; place connector on Manager for shared fan-out or individual servers for selective scope.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish unknown-host on-demand registration, inventory polling, per-connect health revalidation, application inventory and Manager fan-out; interpret Last Poll versus Last Successful Poll.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint/captive portal with on-demand lookup branch; MDM API and scheduled inventory poll; host database/health state; optional Manager fan-out; NAC policy boundary.

records.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 vulnerability-scanner integration: scan thresholds to network enforcement
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 service connectors poll Tenable or Qualys for completed vulnerability scan results; per-scan severity thresholds drive host pass/fail events and optional Host Security actions.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Scanner executes scan -> FortiNAC-F connector polls vendor API -> completed results are matched to target host -> threshold evaluation -> Vulnerability Scan Passed/Failed or integration event -> alarm mapping/Admin Scan -> At Risk/Safe and remediation portal; exception group bypasses normal access enforcement.
records.failure_class: Scanner not run; target IP absent from Qualys Asset Address Management; API connection failure; concurrent/periodic API limit; threshold misconfigured; scan result skipped/incomplete; exception group masks failure in Host View.
records.evidence_pattern: Test Connection proves API path only; Poll and vendor scan history prove result availability; Last Vulnerability Scan/Status/Details/Source show processed host result; distinct events identify incomplete, skipped, refused, connection, and rate-limit boundaries.
records.remediation_path: Validate vendor URL and credentials; run the scan at the vendor; include Qualys target IP in Asset Address Management; poll after completion; tune repetition rate to API limits; validate thresholds and alarm mappings; inspect exception group before treating Passed as a clean scan.
records.question_fingerprint: differentiate connector health from scan execution/result ingestion; interpret Qualys asset refusal and API limits; map failed/passed events to At Risk/Safe; identify exception-group override.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Tenable/Qualys scanner -> FortiNAC-F API connector/poll -> scan threshold evaluation -> events/alarm mapping -> host risk/remediation; exception bypass branch.

records.lesson_subject: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 REST API bulk local-user operations and request correlation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 8.0 REST API adds collection-level POST/DELETE for multiple local users, a users listing field, custom1/custom2/custom3 filters, expanded CSV filters and optional X-Request-ID correlation across read/write operations.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Automation authenticates with dedicated API admin/key over HTTPS -> submits localusers collection request with unique X-Request-ID -> FAC processes request -> response metadata echoes request_id -> GET/filter read-after-write verifies cohort -> downstream RADIUS/group/certificate bindings are validated separately.
records.failure_class: Ambiguous timeout followed by unsafe duplicate POST/DELETE; malformed/oversized request ID; API key or API-admin permission failure; bulk user operation succeeds but attributes/group bindings are wrong; separate CSV import clears RADIUS certificate binding.
records.evidence_pattern: HTTP response and meta.request_id; GET /localusers/ objects filtered by custom fields; API/server log correlation; Local Users record, group and RADIUS attribute/certificate-binding checks; Access-Accept confirms downstream authorization. Request ID is correlation, not idempotency or authentication.
records.remediation_path: Use dedicated API admin and TLS certificate validation; assign a unique <=64-character ASCII request ID; use version-matched batch schema; export/record target cohort; read after write before retry; verify user state, group, RADIUS attributes and certificate binding; treat CSV import as a separate operation.
records.question_fingerprint: select collection-level POST/DELETE; identify X-Request-ID constraints and echoed response metadata; distinguish CSV import defect from REST batch behavior; verify user state and downstream RADIUS authorization.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Automation client -> API admin/key and HTTPS -> localusers collection batch operation -> response meta/request ID and server logs; GET custom-field read-after-write -> separate RADIUS/group validation.

records.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 JIT privilege via secret checkout/check-in: WinRM PowerShell elevation and de-elevation
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 attaches PowerShell checkout/check-in scripts to a secret; resolves privileged target account; connects over WinRM; adds user to elevated group at checkout and removes at check-in; script failure warns but does not block checkout/check-in.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User checks out secret; FortiPAM resolves target admin credential; WinRM executes Add-LocalGroupMember/Add-ADGroupMember; user signs out/in to refresh token; work proceeds; check-in executes removal script; user signs out/in again.
records.failure_class: WinRM disabled/unreachable; privileged credential lacks rights; script/identity variable incorrect; script failure while checkout continues; token not refreshed after membership change; check-in skipped.
records.evidence_pattern: Secret activity shows script result; WinRM service/listener prove reachability; local/AD group membership proves privilege; current logon token may not reflect membership until new logon; checkout alone does not prove elevation.
records.remediation_path: Enable WinRM and verify service; test scripts; ensure privileged account has minimum group rights; inspect activity logs and membership; force sign-out/in after both transitions; monitor overdue checkouts and failed check-ins.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish script execution from token refresh and explain why checkout may succeed while JIT elevation failed.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM checkout -> credential resolver -> WinRM PowerShell add-group -> new logon token -> check-in remove-group -> refreshed least-privilege token.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM Supervisor HA CMDB replication: Patroni timeline divergence, stale PostgreSQL replicas and safe reinitialization
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSIEM Supervisor HA uses PostgreSQL Patroni for CMDB replication and etcd for leader election; failover changes timeline; replica on incompatible timeline can remain running/read-only but stop streaming and leave CMDB stale.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Leader writes CMDB WAL; Patroni streams WAL to replicas; failover elects new leader and advances timeline; valid replicas follow; divergent replica stops applying WAL; detect via Patroni/pg_stat_replication/history; reinitialize only affected replica from healthy leader.
records.failure_class: Replica running but not streaming after timeline change; health replication widget appears Normal; stale CMDB shows deleted devices/collectors; rebuilding from wrong node or without healthy leader risks data loss.
records.evidence_pattern: patronictl list shows role/state/TL/lag; patronictl history shows timeline; pg_stat_replication shows streaming; pg_is_in_recovery identifies replica; compare ph_device counts and phshowVersion.sh; WAL timeline errors show divergence.
records.remediation_path: Confirm healthy leader and streaming replica with lag 0; inspect timeline/history; run patronictl reinit only on affected replica, never leader; monitor same timeline/streaming/lag 0; restart phxctl services; if reinit fails collect Patroni/PostgreSQL logs and stop retrying.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish running from streaming replica and identify safe target/preconditions for Patroni reinit.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: three Supervisor nodes with PostgreSQL Patroni leader/WAL stream; failover timeline branch; stale replica isolated and reinitialized from healthy leader.

records.lesson_subject: FortiSASE regional compliance geofencing: DNS-based source location, ordered tunnel selection and health-check failover
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE determines remote-user country/region from public-IP/DNS location context, applies Regional access allow/deny, selects matching Regional compliance rule and ordered on-prem/PoP connections; on-prem gateways are ICMP health-checked every 1-2 minutes and DNS failover uses 300-second TTL.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiClient resolves turbo FQDN via recursive DNS; FortiSASE determines region; geofencing gate runs; regional rule selects ordered connections; FortiClient attempts priority list; failed on-prem gateway health check updates DNS to next target; endpoint retries after cache expiry.
records.failure_class: Recursive resolver is outside user's country; eDNS client-subnet absent; regional-access gate blocks before rule; fallback PoP omitted; on-prem gateway blocks ICMP; DNS cache delays failover.
records.evidence_pattern: nslookup turbo FQDN shows PoP hostname; nslookup whoami.akamai.com identifies recursive resolver egress; TXT eDNS query reveals client subnet; ICMP and 300-second TTL explain 3-8 minute failover; portal configuration success does not prove resolver-based location.
records.remediation_path: Use in-country recursive resolver and eDNS client-subnet; compare resolver egress to endpoint; check Regional access before rule; order permitted connections and include fallback PoP; permit ICMP to on-prem gateway; allow for DNS TTL.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish endpoint public IP from recursive resolver location and explain unexpected PoP selection despite a valid regional rule.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: remote endpoint -> recursive DNS/eDNS location -> geofencing gate -> regional priority list -> PoP/on-prem tunnel candidates with ICMP/DNS failover.

records.lesson_subject: FortiOS 8.0 SD-WAN speed-test scheduling: backend coordination and interface bandwidth-bound result shaping
records.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 coordinates scheduled SD-WAN speed tests between FortiGate and backend; explicit retry/retry-pause settings removed; test traffic bypasses interface shaping but uses update-inbandwidth/outbandwidth min/max values; result-to-interface-shaping settings moved to interface configuration.
records.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Configure system speed-test-schedule per interface with bounds; FortiGate/backend coordinate test timing; test measures bandwidth; min/max clamp results; interface consumes updated bandwidth values for shaping.
records.failure_class: Obsolete retry commands carried forward; operator expects interface shaper to govern speed-test packets; result settings left in old location; min/max bounds mistaken for measured values.
records.evidence_pattern: show system speed-test-schedule displays interface schedule/bounds; 8.0 CLI no longer exposes retry/retry-pause; compare raw and bounded results and interface shaping settings; completed test does not prove application traffic shaping.
records.remediation_path: Use 8.0 interface-based settings; remove retry/retry-pause assumptions; set min/max bounds intentionally; verify backend coordination and per-interface schedule; test speed-test traffic separately from ordinary shaped traffic.
records.question_fingerprint: distinguish backend retry coordination, bypassed interface shaping and min/max result clamping.
records.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: interface schedule -> backend coordination -> speed-test measurement -> min/max clamp -> shaping consumer; test packets bypass interface shaper.
